reason: The dehumidifier collects cabin moisture, so connecting the hose seems like a first step toward returning it to the roots.
expectation: I expect a hose connected to the dehumidifier, perhaps carrying collected water; I am unsure whether it will need processing first.

alternatives.reason: A pump could move recovered water, but collecting it seems the earlier step.

effect: The hose produced collected condensate, so I can now treat the recovered water.
reaction: The result is straightforward; I am curious what treatment it needs.
reason: The water processor seems the natural next stop before using condensate for plants.
expectation: I expect processed recovered water suitable for the growing system, though the result may need nutrients added.

alternatives.reason: The pump and hose may form a delivery line, but I want to process the collected water first.

effect: Processing yields clean water, ready to mix for the roots.
reaction: That confirms the expected treatment step, though it does not say what was removed.
reason: The growing troughs previously used nutrient solution, so adding concentrate makes the recovered water useful to them.
expectation: I expect a recovered-water nutrient solution.

alternatives.reason: A pump line may also be needed, but the water still needs nutrients.

effect: The clean water is now recycled nutrient solution; I still need a way to deliver it.
reaction: Mixing it is sensible, though familiar from the earlier growing setup.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and a pump and hose could move the solution to the roots.
expectation: I expect a pumped circulation line, though I do not yet know how it connects to the troughs.

effect: The pump and hose make an aerating return loop, suggesting circulation also supplies air.
reaction: The aeration aspect is a useful detail I had not predicted.
reason: Combining the solution with the loop is the only offered action and should complete the return to the roots.
expectation: I expect the recycled solution to circulate through the growing system and satisfy the goal.

effect: The solution and loop became a recirculating reservoir and completed the moisture recovery goal.
reaction: It is satisfying to close the water loop, although the final result gives little sense of it operating.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the aerating return loop gave the water reuse system a physical component and suggested that roots need air as well as solution.

leastWorthwhile.text: Processing the condensate was plausible but the clean-water result did not explain what the processor removed or why treatment was needed.

surprise.text: The pump and hose made an aerating loop; I had anticipated circulation but not aeration.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the connection from the finished reservoir to the roots was implicit rather than shown.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue to see how the growing system and expedition develop, though this chapter's mostly sequential combinations gave me limited decisions to explore.
